stem: What is a test cross?

options.content: Crossing an individual of unknown genotype with a homozygous recessive
options.rationale: Correct.

options.content: Crossing two heterozygous individuals to obtain an F2 generation
options.rationale: That is an F1 × F1 cross.

options.content: Crossing two pure-breeding parents with contrasting phenotypes
options.rationale: That produces the F1 generation.

options.content: Crossing an individual of unknown genotype with a homozygous dominant one
options.rationale: A homozygous dominant parent would hide the unknown alleles.

explanation: A test cross uses a **homozygous recessive** partner, whose gametes all carry the recessive allele.

stem: Two roan cattle ($C^R C^W$) are crossed. What proportion of the offspring is expected to be roan?

options.rationale: 1/4 is the proportion of red, or of white.
3/4 would apply with complete dominance.
Correct: 1 red : 2 roan : 1 white.

options.content: All of them
options.rationale: Only a red × white cross gives all roan.

explanation: $C^R C^W \times C^R C^W$ gives 1 $C^R C^R$ : 2 $C^R C^W$ : 1 $C^W C^W$, so half are roan.

stem: A man of blood group AB and a woman of blood group O have children. Which blood groups are possible among the children?

options.content: A and B only
options.rationale: Correct: $I^A I^O$ or $I^B I^O$.

options.content: AB and O only
options.rationale: Each child gets $I^O$ from the mother and either $I^A$ or $I^B$ from the father.

options.content: A, B, AB and O
options.rationale: AB and O are impossible here.

options.content: A, B and O only
options.rationale: No child can be $I^O I^O$, as the father has no $I^O$.

explanation: Father's gametes $I^A$ or $I^B$; mother's all $I^O$: children $I^A I^O$ (A) or $I^B I^O$ (B).

stem: Which term describes an organism with two different alleles of a gene?

options.content: Homozygous
options.rationale: Homozygous means two identical alleles.

options.content: Codominant
options.rationale: Codominant describes alleles, not the organism's genotype.

options.content: Heterozygous
options.rationale: Correct.

options.content: Haploid
options.rationale: Haploid cells have only one set of chromosomes.

explanation: Two different alleles: **heterozygous**.

stem: In a test cross, a tall pea plant crossed with a dwarf plant gives 46 tall and 41 dwarf offspring. What was the genotype of the tall parent?

options.content: Homozygous dominant, TT
options.rationale: TT would give only tall offspring.

options.content: Heterozygous, with one of each allele
options.rationale: Correct: a ratio close to 1 : 1.

options.content: Homozygous recessive, tt
options.rationale: A tt plant would be dwarf, not tall.

options.content: Either genotype, so it cannot be decided from these data
options.rationale: The dwarf offspring prove it carries t.

explanation: Dwarf offspring (tt) need a t from each parent, so the tall parent is **Tt**; the ratio is close to 1 : 1.
hints: Where did the dwarf offspring get their alleles from?

stem: Two unaffected parents have a child with albinism (a recessive condition). What is the probability that their next child will be unaffected?

options.rationale: This is the probability of an affected child.
This would apply to Aa × aa.
This is the chance that an unaffected child is a carrier.
Correct: both parents must be Aa.

explanation: Both parents are Aa; Aa × Aa gives 3/4 unaffected. Each child is independent of the last.
hints: Work out the parents' genotypes first.

stem: Two heterozygous tall pea plants (Tt) are crossed. One of the tall offspring is chosen at random. What is the probability that it is heterozygous?

options.rationale: 1/2 of ALL offspring are Tt, but the dwarf ones are excluded here.
1/4 is the proportion of TT among all offspring.
3/4 is the proportion of all offspring that are tall.
Correct: of 3 tall plants, 2 are Tt.

explanation: Tall offspring are 1 TT : 2 Tt, so P(Tt | tall) = 2/3.
hints: Leave out the dwarf plants, which are already excluded.

stem: Why is the genotype ratio the same as the phenotype ratio in the F2 of a cross involving codominant alleles?

options.content: Codominant alleles are always found on sex chromosomes
options.rationale: Codominant alleles can be on any chromosome.

options.content: No heterozygotes are produced in the F2 generation
options.rationale: Half the F2 are heterozygous.

options.content: Each genotype produces a different phenotype
options.rationale: Correct: the heterozygote has its own phenotype.

options.content: Codominant alleles do not separate when gametes form
options.rationale: Alleles separate in meiosis as usual.

explanation: Because both alleles are expressed, the heterozygote is distinguishable: 1 : 2 : 1 genotypes and phenotypes.
hints: Can you tell a heterozygote from a homozygote by its phenotype?

stem: A gamete from a heterozygous parent (Tt) carries both alleles, T and t.
explanation: False. Gametes are haploid; each carries one allele, T or t.

stem: If two carriers of a recessive condition already have one affected child, the probability that their next child is affected is still 1/4.
explanation: True. Each fertilisation is an independent event.

stem: Match each ABO genotype with the blood group it gives.
explanation: $I^A$ and $I^B$ are codominant, both dominant to $I^O$.

stem: Choose the correct words.

payload.template: The ABO gene is an example of {{blank:a}} alleles. Alleles $I^A$ and $I^B$ are {{blank:b}}, and both are {{blank:c}} to $I^O$.

explanation: Multiple alleles; $I^A$, $I^B$ codominant; both dominant to $I^O$.

stem: Give the term for a relationship between two alleles in which both are expressed in the phenotype of a heterozygote.
explanation: **Codominance**.

stem: Two Tt pea plants are crossed and 312 offspring are grown. How many dwarf plants are expected?
explanation: Expected ratio 3 tall : 1 dwarf, so dwarf = 312 ÷ 4 = **78**.
workedSolution: 1. Expected ratio 3 tall : 1 dwarf, so dwarf = 312 ÷ 4 = **78**.

stem: A couple are both $I^B I^O$. Calculate the percentage probability that their first two children both have blood group O. Give your answer to two decimal places.
explanation:
1. Each child: $P(I^O I^O) = \dfrac{1}{4}$.
2. The children are independent, so multiply: $\dfrac{1}{4} \times \dfrac{1}{4} = \dfrac{1}{16} = 0.0625$.
3. As a percentage: $6.25\%$. Adding the probabilities (50%) is wrong; so is giving the chance for one child only (25%).
workedSolution:
1. Each child: $P(I^O I^O) = \dfrac{1}{4}$.
2. The children are independent, so multiply: $\dfrac{1}{4} \times \dfrac{1}{4} = \dfrac{1}{16} = 0.0625$.
3. As a percentage: $6.25\%$. Adding the probabilities (50%) is wrong; so is giving the chance for one child only (25%).
hints: Find the probability for one child.

stem: In snapdragons, flower colour is controlled by two codominant alleles: $C^R$ (red) and $C^W$ (white); heterozygotes are pink. Use a genetic diagram to show the result of crossing two pink plants.

points.description: Parent phenotypes pink × pink and genotypes $C^R C^W$ × $C^R C^W$
Punnett square / offspring genotypes $C^R C^R$, $C^R C^W$, $C^R C^W$, $C^W C^W$
Phenotypes linked to genotypes: red, pink, pink, white

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Parent phenotypes: pink × pink. Parent genotypes: $C^R C^W$ × $C^R C^W$. Gametes: $C^R$, $C^W$ from each. Punnett square gives $C^R C^R$ (red), $C^R C^W$ (pink), $C^R C^W$ (pink) and $C^W C^W$ (white). Ratio 1 red : 2 pink : 1 white.

explanation: Full genetic diagram with a 1 : 2 : 1 ratio.
hints: Set out every line of the diagram.

stem: Explain how a test cross can show whether a black guinea pig is homozygous (BB) or heterozygous (Bb), where black is dominant to white.

points.description: Cross the black guinea pig with a white (homozygous recessive, bb) one
bb parent gives only b gametes, so the offspring phenotype shows the allele from the black parent
All black offspring: BB (probably); any white offspring / about 1 : 1: Bb

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Cross the black guinea pig with a white one, which must be bb. All its gametes carry b, so each offspring's colour shows which allele it received from the black parent. If all offspring are black (in a large litter) the black parent is probably BB; if any are white, with about half black and half white, it is Bb.

explanation: Homozygous recessive partner reveals the alleles.
hints: Which gametes does the white parent make?

stem: In a family, two parents with Huntington's disease have a daughter who does not have the disease. Explain what this shows about the allele, and give the genotypes of all three people.

points.description: Unaffected child from two affected parents, so the allele must be dominant

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: If the disease allele were recessive, both affected parents would be homozygous recessive and could only have affected children. An unaffected child from two affected parents shows the disease allele is dominant (H). Both parents must be heterozygous, Hh, and each passed on h, so the daughter is hh.

explanation: Unaffected child of two affected parents → dominant allele.
hints: What would happen if the allele were recessive?

stem: A pedigree for a condition caused by one gene is described below. Generation I: man I-1 (unaffected) and woman I-2 (unaffected). Generation II: their children II-1 (unaffected son), II-2 (affected daughter) and II-3 (unaffected son). II-3 marries II-4, an affected woman from another family. Generation III: their children III-1 (unaffected daughter) and III-2 (affected son).

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Which statement about the allele causing the condition is correct?

options.content: It is dominant, because III-2 is affected like his mother
options.rationale: An affected child of unaffected parents (II-2) rules out a dominant allele.

options.content: It is recessive, because II-2 is affected but neither parent is
options.rationale: Correct.

options.content: It is codominant, because affected and unaffected people occur
options.rationale: Codominance is not shown by this pedigree.

options.content: It cannot be decided from this pedigree
options.rationale: The parents I-1, I-2 and child II-2 decide it.

parts.explanation: Two unaffected parents with an affected child: recessive.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Using D and d, give the genotype of I-2.
parts.explanation: I-2 must carry d to have an affected daughter, but is unaffected: Dd.

parts.label: (c)
parts.explanation: II-3 has an affected son (dd), so must carry d: Dd.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Calculate the probability, as a percentage, that the next child of II-3 and II-4 will be affected.
parts.explanation: Dd × dd gives 1 Dd : 1 dd, so 50%.
parts.workedSolution: 1. Dd × dd gives 1 Dd : 1 dd, so 50%.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Before II-3 had children, what was the probability that he was a carrier? Explain.

points.description: Parents Dd × Dd give 1 DD : 2 Dd : 1 dd; he is unaffected so dd is excluded, leaving 2 of 3

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: 2/3. His parents were both Dd, giving 1 DD : 2 Dd : 1 dd. As he is unaffected he cannot be dd, so 2 of the 3 remaining outcomes are Dd.

explanation: Pedigree logic: affected child of unaffected parents shows a recessive allele.
hints: Start with I-1, I-2 and II-2.

stem:
A farmer near Chinhoyi crossed roan bulls with roan cows over several years. The calves were recorded.

| Coat colour | Number of calves |
|---|---|
| Red | 58 |
| Roan | 121 |
| White | 61 |

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Using the symbols $C^R$ and $C^W$, draw a genetic diagram (described in words) to explain these results.

points.description: Parents roan × roan, genotypes $C^R C^W$ × $C^R C^W$
Offspring $C^R C^R$ red, $C^R C^W$ roan, $C^W C^W$ white

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Parents: roan × roan, $C^R C^W$ × $C^R C^W$. Gametes: $C^R$, $C^W$ from each. Offspring: 1 $C^R C^R$ (red) : 2 $C^R C^W$ (roan) : 1 $C^W C^W$ (white).

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the expected number of roan calves.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Explain why the observed numbers are not exactly the same as the expected numbers.

points.description: Fertilisation is random / which gametes fuse is a matter of chance

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Which gametes fuse at fertilisation is random, so observed numbers vary by chance around the expected ratio.

explanation: Roan × roan: 1 : 2 : 1.
